Could add or delete docker desktop mcps, depending on list from gateway\n    - claude mcp remove <name> - remove a server (NPM, or docker hub)\n    - claude mcp list - list servers\n",

│      │                           │ within a directory. Only works within     │
│      │                           │ allowed directories.                      │
│  8   │ directory_tree            │ Get a recursive tree view of files and    │
│      │                           │ directories as a JSON structure. Each     │
│      │                           │ entry includes 'name', 'type'             │
│      │                           │ (file/directory), and 'children' for      │
│      │                           │ directories. Files have no children       │
│      │                           │ array, while directories always have a    │
│      │                           │ children array (which may be empty). The  │
│      │                           │ output is formatted with 2-space          │
│      │                           │ indentation for readability. Only works   │
│      │                           │ within allowed directories.               │
│  9   │ move_file                 │ Move or rename files and directories. Can │
│      │                           │ move files between directories and rename │
│      │                           │ them in a single operation. If the        │
│      │                           │ destination exists, the operation will    │
│      │                           │ fail. Works across different directories  │
│      │                           │ and can be used for simple renaming       │
│      │                           │ within the same directory. Both source    │
│      │                           │ and destination must be within allowed    │
│      │                           │ directories.                              │
│  10  │ search_files              │ Recursively search for files and          │
│      │                           │ directories matching a pattern. Searches  │
│      │                           │ through all subdirectories from the       │
│      │                           │ starting path. The search is              │
│      │                           │ case-insensitive and matches partial      │
│      │                           │ names. Returns full paths to all matching │
│      │                           │ items. Great for finding files when you   │
│      │                           │ don't know their exact location. Only     │
│      │                           │ searches within allowed directories.      │
│  11  │ get_file_info             │ Retrieve detailed metadata about a file   │
│      │                           │ or directory. Returns comprehensive       │
│      │                           │ information including size, creation      │
│      │                           │ time, last modified time, permissions,    │
│      │                           │ and type. This tool is perfect for        │
│      │                           │ understanding file characteristics        │
│      │                           │ without reading the actual content. Only  │
│      │                           │ works within allowed directories.         │
│  12  │ list_allowed_directories  │ Returns the list of directories that this │
│      │                           │ server is allowed to access. Use this to  │
│      │                           │ understand which directories are          │
│      │                           │ available before trying to access files.  │

   350→        console.print("[dim]   Example: [cyan]mcp-manager install-package modelcontextprotocol-filesystem[/cyan][/dim]")
   351→        
   352→    except Exception as e:
   353→        console.print(f"[red]✗[/red] Failed to discover servers: {e}")
   354→

   356→
   357→def handle_errors(func):
   358→    """Decorator to handle common CLI errors."""
   359→    import functools
   360→    
   361→    @functools.wraps(func)
   362→    def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
   363→        try:
   364→            return func(*args, **kwargs)
   365→        except MCPManagerError as e:
   366→            console.print(f"[red]Error:[/red] {e}")
   367→            sys.exit(1)
   368→        except KeyboardInterrupt:
   369→            console.print("\n[yellow]Operation cancelled by user[/yellow]")
   370→            sys.exit(130)
   371→        except Exception as e:
   372→            console.print(f"[red]Unexpected error:[/red] {e}")
   373→            if logger.isEnabledFor(10):  # DEBUG level
   374→                console.print_exception()
   375→            sys.exit(1)
   376→    return wrapper

   512→@cli.command()
   513→@click.argument("name")
   514→@click.argument("command", required=False)
   515→@click.option(
   516→    "--scope",
   517→    type=click.Choice([s.value for s in ServerScope], case_sensitive=False),
   518→    default=ServerScope.USER.value,
   519→    help="Configuration scope"
   520→)
   521→@click.option(
   522→    "--type",
   523→    "server_type",
   524→    type=click.Choice([t.value for t in ServerType], case_sensitive=False),
   525→    default=ServerType.CUSTOM.value,
   526→    help="Server type"
   527→)
   528→@click.option(
   529→    "--description",
   530→    help="Server description"
   531→)
   532→@click.option(
   533→    "--env",
   534→    multiple=True,
   535→    help="Environment variables (KEY=VALUE)"
   536→)
   537→@click.option(
   538→    "--arg",
   539→    "args",
   540→    multiple=True,
   541→    help="Command arguments"
   542→)
   543→@handle_errors
   544→def add(
   545→    name: str,
   546→    command: str, 
   547→    scope: str,
   548→    server_type: str,
   549→    description: Optional[str],
   550→    env: List[str],
   551→    args: List[str],
   552→):
   553→    """Add a new MCP server."""
   554→    manager = cli_context.get_manager()
   555→    
   556→    # Add server using simple manager
   557→    async def add_server_async():
   558→        try:
   559→            if server_type:
   560→                detected_server_type = server_type
   561→            else:
   562→                # Auto-detect server type based on command
   563→                if command == 'npx':
   564→                    detected_server_type = ServerType.NPM
   565→                elif command.endswith('/docker') or command == 'docker':
   566→                    detected_server_type = ServerType.DOCKER
   567→                else:
   568→                    detected_server_type = ServerType.CUSTOM
   569→            
   570→            # Check for similar servers first (don't treat as error)
   571→            similar_servers = await manager.check_for_similar_servers(
   572→                name=name,
   573→                server_type=detected_server_type,
   574→                command=command,
   575→                args=args
   576→            )
   577→            
   578→            # If similar servers found, warn user and ask for confirmation
   579→            if similar_servers:
   580→                console.print(f"[yellow]⚠ Warning:[/yellow] Found {len(similar_servers)} similar server(s) that might provide the same functionality:")
   581→                
   582→                for similar_info in similar_servers:
   583→                    similar_server = similar_info["server"]
   584→                    score = similar_info["similarity_score"]
   585→                    reasons = similar_info["reasons"]
   586→                    recommendation = similar_info["recommendation"]
   587→                    server_type_str = similar_server.server_type.value if hasattr(similar_server.server_type, 'value') else str(similar_server.server_type)
   588→                    
   589→                    console.print(f"  • [cyan]{similar_server.name}[/cyan] ({server_type_str}) - Similarity: {score}%")
   590→                    console.print(f"    [dim]Reasons: {', '.join(reasons)}[/dim]")
   591→                    console.print(f"    [dim]Recommendation: {recommendation}[/dim]")
   592→                
   593→                console.print(f"\n[yellow]Installing multiple servers for the same functionality may cause conflicts.[/yellow]")
   594→                console.print(f"[yellow]Do you accept the risks and want to continue?[/yellow]")
   595→                
   596→                from rich.prompt import Confirm
   597→                try:
   598→                    if not Confirm.ask("Continue with installation?"):
   599→                        console.print("[dim]Installation cancelled by user[/dim]")
   600→                        return
   601→                except (EOFError, KeyboardInterrupt):
   602→                    console.print("[dim]Installation cancelled (non-interactive terminal)[/dim]")
   603→                    return
   604→            
   605→            # Proceed with installation (no duplicate checking since we handled it above)
   606→            server = await manager.add_server(
   607→                name=name,
   608→                server_type=detected_server_type,
   609→                command=command,
   610→                args=args
   611→            )
   612→            console.print(f"✅ Successfully added server: {name}")
   613→                
   614→        except Exception as e:
   615→            console.print(f"❌ Failed to add server {name}: {e}")
   616→    
   617→    asyncio.run(add_server_async())

   675→@cli.command()
   676→@click.option(
   677→    "--query", "-q",
   678→    help="Search query (supports wildcards like 'aws*' and regex like 'regex:^file.*')"
   679→)
   680→@click.option(
   681→    "--type",
   682→    "server_type",
   683→    type=click.Choice([t.value for t in ServerType], case_sensitive=False),
   684→    help="Server type filter"
   685→)
   686→@click.option(
   687→    "--limit", "-l",
   688→    type=int,
   689→    default=20,
   690→    help="Maximum results"
   691→)
   692→@click.option(
   693→    "--update-catalog", 
   694→    is_flag=True,
   695→    help="Update Docker MCP catalog before discovery"
   696→)
   697→@handle_errors
   698→def discover(query: Optional[str], server_type: Optional[str], limit: int, update_catalog: bool):
   699→    """
   700→    Discover available MCP servers with pattern matching support.
   701→    
   702→    Query supports:
   703→    - Wildcards: 'aws*' matches aws-s3, aws-dynamodb, etc.
   704→    - Regex: 'regex:^file.*server$' for advanced patterns
   705→    - Simple text: 'filesystem' for substring matching
   706→    """
   707→    discovery = cli_context.get_discovery()
   708→    
   709→    type_filter = ServerType(server_type) if server_type else None
   710→    
   711→    # Run async discovery
   712→    async def run_discovery():
   713→        # Update catalog if requested
   714→        if update_catalog:
   715→            console.print("[blue]Updating Docker MCP catalog...[/blue]")
   716→            success = await discovery.update_docker_catalog()
   717→            if success:
   718→                console.print("[green]✅ Docker MCP catalog updated[/green]")
   719→            else:
   720→                console.print("[yellow]⚠️ Failed to update Docker MCP catalog[/yellow]")
   721→        
   722→        return await discovery.discover_servers(
   723→            query=query,
   724→            server_type=type_filter,
   725→            limit=limit
   726→        )
   727→        
   728→    results = asyncio.run(run_discovery())
   729→    
   730→    if not results:
   731→        console.print("[yellow]No servers found[/yellow]")
   732→        return
   733→        
   734→    table = Table(title="Available MCP Servers", show_header=True, header_style="bold blue")
   735→    table.add_column("Install ID", style="cyan", width=20)
   736→    table.add_column("Type", justify="center", width=15)
   737→    table.add_column("Description", style="dim", width=30)
   738→    table.add_column("Package", style="green", width=25)
   739→    table.add_column("Install Command", style="yellow", width=30)
   740→    
   741→    for result in results:
   742→        # Create unique install ID - use same logic as in install-package command
   743→        install_id = _generate_install_id(result)
   744→        
   745→        # Create simple install command
   746→        install_cmd = f"mcp-manager install-package {install_id}"
   747→        
   748→        table.add_row(
   749→            install_id,
   750→            result.server_type.value,
   751→            result.description[:30] + "..." if result.description and len(result.description) > 30 else (result.description or ""),
   752→            result.package or "",
   753→            install_cmd
   754→        )
   755→        
   756→    console.print(table)
   757→    
   758→    if results:
   759→        console.print("\n[dim]💡 To install a server, copy the command from the 'Install Command' column[/dim]")
   760→        console.print("[dim]   Example: [cyan]mcp-manager install-package modelcontextprotocol-filesystem[/cyan][/dim]")
   761→
   762→
   763→@cli.command("install-package")
   764→@click.argument("install_id")
   765→@handle_errors
   766→def install_package(install_id: str):
   767→    """Install a server using its unique install ID from discovery."""
   768→    discovery = cli_context.get_discovery()
   769→    manager = cli_context.get_manager()
   770→    
   771→    # Resolve install ID back to package info
   772→    async def find_and_install():
   773→        # Try to extract search terms from install_id to improve discovery
   774→        search_query = None
   775→        if install_id.startswith("dd-"):
   776→            # Docker Desktop server - extract server name
   777→            search_query = install_id[3:]  # Remove 'dd-' prefix
   778→        elif "-" in install_id:
   779→            # Extract likely server name from install_id
   780→            search_query = install_id.split("-")[-1]  # Take last part
   781→            
   782→        # Search with higher limits to ensure we find all servers
   783→        # Try with query first, then without query as fallback
   784→        target_result = None
   785→        
   786→        for query_attempt in [search_query, None]:
   787→            results = await discovery.discover_servers(
   788→                query=query_attempt, 
   789→                limit=200  # Higher limit to ensure we find all servers
   790→            )
   791→            
   792→            for result in results:
   793→                # Generate install_id using same logic as discover command
   794→                result_id = _generate_install_id(result)
   795→                
   796→                if result_id == install_id:
   797→                    target_result = result
   798→                    break
   799→            
   800→            if target_result:
   801→                break
   802→        
   803→        if not target_result:
   804→            console.print(f"[red]✗[/red] Install ID '{install_id}' not found")
   805→            console.print("[yellow]💡[/yellow] Run [cyan]mcp-manager discover[/cyan] to see available install IDs")
   806→            return
   807→        
   808→        # Create unique server name to avoid conflicts
   809→        if target_result.server_type == ServerType.NPM:
   810→            server_name = install_id.replace("modelcontextprotocol-", "official-")
   811→        elif target_result.server_type == ServerType.DOCKER:
   812→            server_name = install_id.replace("-", "_")
   813→        elif target_result.server_type == ServerType.DOCKER_DESKTOP:
   814→            # For Docker Desktop, use the actual server name (remove dd- prefix)
   815→            server_name = install_id.replace("dd-", "")
   816→        else:
   817→            server_name = install_id
   818→        
   819→        console.print(f"[blue]Installing[/blue] {target_result.package} as [cyan]{server_name}[/cyan]")
   820→        
   821→        # Check if server already exists
   822→        existing_servers = await manager.list_servers()
   823→        if any(s.name == server_name for s in existing_servers):
   824→            console.print(f"[yellow]⚠[/yellow] Server '{server_name}' already exists")
   825→            from rich.prompt import Confirm
   826→            if not Confirm.ask("Replace existing server?"):
   827→                console.print("[dim]Installation cancelled[/dim]")
   828→                return
   829→        
   830→        # Check for similar servers that might provide the same functionality
   831→        try:
   832→            existing_servers = await manager.list_servers()
   833→            similar_servers = discovery.detect_similar_servers(target_result, existing_servers)
   834→            
   835→            if similar_servers:
   836→                console.print(f"[yellow]⚠[/yellow] Found {len(similar_servers)} similar server(s) that might provide the same functionality:")
   837→                for similar_info in similar_servers:
   838→                    similar_server = similar_info["server"]
   839→                    score = similar_info["similarity_score"]
   840→                    reasons = similar_info["reasons"]
   841→                    recommendation = similar_info["recommendation"]
   842→                    
   843→                    console.print(f"  • [cyan]{similar_server.name}[/cyan] ({similar_server.server_type.value}) - Similarity: {score}%")
   844→                    console.print(f"    [dim]Reasons: {', '.join(reasons)}[/dim]")
   845→                    console.print(f"    [dim]Recommendation: {recommendation}[/dim]")
   846→                
   847→                console.print(f"\n[yellow]Installing multiple servers for the same functionality may cause conflicts.[/yellow]")
   848→                from rich.prompt import Confirm
   849→                if not Confirm.ask("Continue anyway?"):
   850→                    console.print("[dim]Installation cancelled[/dim]")
   851→                    return
   852→        except Exception as e:
   853→            logger.debug(f"Failed to check for similar servers: {e}")
   854→            # Continue with installation even if similarity check fails
   855→        
   856→        # Check if server needs additional configuration
   857→        install_args = target_result.install_args or []
   858→        additional_config = _prompt_for_server_configuration(
   859→            server_name=server_name,
   860→            server_type=target_result.server_type,
   861→            package=target_result.package
   862→        )
   863→        
   864→        if additional_config:
   865→            # For Docker Desktop servers, update the config file
   866→            if target_result.server_type == ServerType.DOCKER_DESKTOP:
   867→                _update_docker_mcp_config(server_name, additional_config)
   868→            else:
   869→                # For other servers, add to install args
   870→                install_args.extend(additional_config.get('args', []))
   871→        
   872→        # Install the server
   873→        try:
   874→            server = await manager.add_server(
   875→                name=server_name,
   876→                server_type=target_result.server_type,
   877→                command=target_result.install_command,
   878→                description=target_result.description,
   879→                args=install_args
   880→            )
   881→            console.print(f"[green]✓[/green] Installed server: {server.name}")
   882→            console.print("[dim]Server is now active in Claude Code![/dim]")
   883→            
   884→            # Ask if user wants to view server details
   885→            from rich.prompt import Confirm
   886→            if Confirm.ask(f"\n[cyan]View details for '{server.name}'?[/cyan]", default=True):
   887→                # Show server details
   888→                await _show_server_details_after_install(manager, server.name)
   889→                
   890→                # Wait for user to press Enter
   891→                console.print("\n[dim]Press Enter to continue...[/dim]", end="")
   892→                input()
   893→            
   894→            # Ask if user wants to search for another server
   895→            if Confirm.ask(f"\n[cyan]Search for another server to install?[/cyan]", default=False):
   896→                console.print("")  # Add spacing
   897→                # Show discovery results
   898→                await _show_discovery_for_next_install(discovery)
   899→            
   900→        except Exception as e:
   901→            console.print(f"[red]✗[/red] Failed to install: {e}")
   902→    
   903→    asyncio.run(find_and_install())
   904→
   905→
   906→@cli.command()
   907→@click.argument("name")
   908→@handle_errors
   909→def install(name: str):
   910→    """Install a server from discovery results."""
   911→    discovery = cli_context.get_discovery()
   912→    manager = cli_context.get_manager()
   913→    
   914→    # Search for the server
   915→    async def find_and_install():
   916→        results = await discovery.discover_servers(query=name, limit=10)
   917→        
   918→        # Find exact match or best match
   919→        exact_match = next((r for r in results if r.name == name), None)
   920→        if not exact_match:
   921→            # Try partial match
   922→            partial_matches = [r for r in results if name.lower() in r.name.lower()]
   923→            if not partial_matches:
   924→                console.print(f"[red]✗[/red] Server '{name}' not found in discovery")
   925→                console.print("[yellow]💡[/yellow] Try: [cyan]mcp-manager discover --query {name}[/cyan]")
   926→                return
   927→            exact_match = partial_matches[0]
   928→            console.print(f"[yellow]ℹ[/yellow] Using closest match: {exact_match.name}")
   929→        
   930→        # Check for similar servers first (don't treat as error)
   931→        similar_servers = await manager.check_for_similar_servers(
   932→            name=exact_match.name,
   933→            server_type=exact_match.server_type,
   934→            command=exact_match.install_command,
   935→            args=[]
   936→        )
   937→        
   938→        # If similar servers found, warn user and ask for confirmation
   939→        if similar_servers:
   940→            console.print(f"[yellow]⚠ Warning:[/yellow] Found {len(similar_servers)} similar server(s) that might provide the same functionality:")
   941→            
   942→            for similar_info in similar_servers:
   943→                similar_server = similar_info["server"]
   944→                score = similar_info["similarity_score"]
   945→                reasons = similar_info["reasons"]
   946→                recommendation = similar_info["recommendation"]
   947→                server_type_str = similar_server.server_type.value if hasattr(similar_server.server_type, 'value') else str(similar_server.server_type)
   948→                
   949→                console.print(f"  • [cyan]{similar_server.name}[/cyan] ({server_type_str}) - Similarity: {score}%")
   950→                console.print(f"    [dim]Reasons: {', '.join(reasons)}[/dim]")
   951→                console.print(f"    [dim]Recommendation: {recommendation}[/dim]")
   952→            
   953→            console.print(f"\n[yellow]Installing multiple servers for the same functionality may cause conflicts.[/yellow]")
   954→            console.print(f"[yellow]Do you accept the risks and want to continue?[/yellow]")
   955→            
   956→            from rich.prompt import Confirm
   957→            try:
   958→                if not Confirm.ask("Continue with installation?"):
   959→                    console.print("[dim]Installation cancelled by user[/dim]")
   960→                    return
   961→            except (EOFError, KeyboardInterrupt):
   962→                console.print("[dim]Installation cancelled (non-interactive terminal)[/dim]")
   963→                return
   964→        
   965→        # Install the server
   966→        server = await manager.add_server(
   967→            name=exact_match.name,
   968→            server_type=exact_match.server_type,
   969→            command=exact_match.install_command,
   970→            description=exact_match.description
   971→        )
   972→        
   973→        console.print(f"[green]✓[/green] Installed server: {server.name}")
   974→        console.print(f"[dim]Command: {exact_match.install_command}[/dim]")
   975→        console.print("\n[green]✓[/green] Server is now active in Claude Code!")
   976→    
   977→    asyncio.run(find_and_install())
   978→

  1078→    # Show detailed information if verbose

  1082→        if sync_result.claude_available:

  1088→        for server in sync_result.manager_servers:
  1089→            console.print(f"    • {server}")
  1090→        
  1091→        console.print(f"  [cyan]Claude servers:[/cyan] {len(sync_result.claude_servers)}")
  1092→        for server in sync_result.claude_servers:
  1093→            console.print(f"    • {server}")
  1094→        
  1095→        if sync_result.missing_in_claude:

  1097→        
  1098→        if sync_result.missing_in_manager:

  1100→    
  1101→    # Exit with error code if not in sync
  1102→    if not sync_result.in_sync:
  1103→        sys.exit(1)

  1189→@cli.command()
  1190→@click.option(
  1191→    "--dry-run", 
  1192→    is_flag=True, 
  1193→    help="Show what would be cleaned up without making changes"
  1194→)
  1195→@click.option(
  1196→    "--no-backup", 
  1197→    is_flag=True, 
  1198→    help="Skip creating backup (not recommended)"
  1199→)
  1200→@handle_errors
  1201→def cleanup(dry_run: bool, no_backup: bool):
  1202→    """Clean up problematic MCP server configurations.
  1203→    
  1204→    This command removes old or broken MCP server configurations that can
  1205→    cause connection errors, such as:
  1206→    - Old Docker commands with incorrect image names
  1207→    - Servers with invalid command formats
  1208→    - Configurations causing ENOENT errors
  1209→    """
  1210→    asyncio.run(_cleanup_impl(dry_run, no_backup))
  1211→
  1212→
  1213→async def _cleanup_impl(dry_run: bool, no_backup: bool):
  1214→    """Implementation of cleanup command."""
  1215→    import json
  1216→    import shutil
  1217→    from datetime import datetime
  1218→    from pathlib import Path
  1219→    
  1220→    console.print("[bold blue]🧹 MCP Configuration Cleanup[/bold blue]")
  1221→    
  1222→    # Check Claude configuration file
  1223→    claude_config = Path.home() / ".claude.json"
  1224→    if not claude_config.exists():
  1225→        console.print("[yellow]No Claude configuration found[/yellow]")
  1226→        return
  1227→    
  1228→    # Create backup unless disabled
  1229→    backup_path = None
  1230→    if not no_backup and not dry_run:
  1231→        timestamp = datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
  1232→        backup_path = claude_config.with_suffix(f".backup_{timestamp}")
  1233→        shutil.copy2(claude_config, backup_path)
  1234→        console.print(f"✅ Created backup: {backup_path}")
  1235→    
  1236→    # Load and analyze configuration
  1237→    try:
  1238→        with open(claude_config) as f:
  1239→            config = json.load(f)
  1240→    except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
  1241→        console.print(f"[red]Error reading Claude configuration: {e}[/red]")
  1242→        return
  1243→    
  1244→    # Find problematic configurations
  1245→    problems_found = []
  1246→    projects_to_clean = {}
  1247→    
  1248→    if "projectConfigs" in config:
  1249→        for project_path, project_config in config["projectConfigs"].items():
  1250→            if "mcpServers" in project_config and project_config["mcpServers"]:
  1251→                servers_to_remove = []
  1252→                
  1253→                for server_name, server_config in project_config["mcpServers"].items():
  1254→                    # Check for problematic Docker commands
  1255→                    command = server_config.get("command", "")
  1256→                    
  1257→                    # Pattern 1: Old incorrect Docker MCP commands
  1258→                    if command.startswith("docker run -i --rm --pull always mcp/"):
  1259→                        problems_found.append(f"❌ {project_path}:{server_name} - Invalid Docker command")
  1260→                        servers_to_remove.append(server_name)
  1261→                    
  1262→                    # Pattern 2: Commands that cause ENOENT
  1263→                    elif "mcp/" in command and "docker run" in command:
  1264→                        problems_found.append(f"⚠️  {project_path}:{server_name} - Likely ENOENT error")
  1265→                        servers_to_remove.append(server_name)
  1266→                
  1267→                if servers_to_remove:
  1268→                    projects_to_clean[project_path] = servers_to_remove
  1269→    
  1270→    # Report findings
  1271→    if not problems_found:
  1272→        console.print("[green]✅ No problematic MCP configurations found[/green]")
  1273→        return
  1274→    
  1275→    console.print(f"\n[yellow]Found {len(problems_found)} problematic configurations:[/yellow]")
  1276→    for problem in problems_found:
  1277→        console.print(f"  {problem}")
  1278→    
  1279→    if dry_run:
  1280→        console.print("\n[blue]🔍 Dry run mode - no changes made[/blue]")
  1281→        return
  1282→    
  1283→    # Apply fixes
  1284→    if projects_to_clean:
  1285→        console.print(f"\n[blue]🔧 Cleaning up configurations...[/blue]")
  1286→        
  1287→        for project_path, servers_to_remove in projects_to_clean.items():
  1288→            for server_name in servers_to_remove:
  1289→                del config["projectConfigs"][project_path]["mcpServers"][server_name]
  1290→                console.print(f"  ✅ Removed {project_path}:{server_name}")
  1291→        
  1292→        # Save updated configuration
  1293→        try:
  1294→            with open(claude_config, 'w') as f:
  1295→                json.dump(config, f, indent=2)
  1296→            console.print(f"\n[green]✅ Configuration cleaned successfully[/green]")
  1297→            if backup_path:
  1298→                console.print(f"[green]📁 Backup saved to: {backup_path}[/green]")
  1299→        except Exception as e:
  1300→            console.print(f"[red]Error saving configuration: {e}[/red]")
  1301→            if backup_path:
  1302→                console.print(f"[yellow]Restoring from backup...[/yellow]")
  1303→                shutil.copy2(backup_path, claude_config)
  1304→
  1305→
  1306→@cli.command("server-details")
  1307→@click.argument("server_name")
  1308→@handle_errors
  1309→def server_details(server_name: str):
  1310→    """Show detailed information about a specific server including its tools.
  1311→    
  1312→    Displays comprehensive information about an MCP server including:
  1313→    - Basic server information (type, status, command)
  1314→    - Available tools and their descriptions
  1315→    - Usage examples for Claude Code
  1316→    
  1317→    Example:
  1318→      mcp-manager server-details SQLite
  1319→      mcp-manager server-details filesystem
  1320→    """
  1321→    asyncio.run(_server_details_impl(server_name))
  1322→
  1323→
  1324→async def _server_details_impl(server_name: str):
  1325→    """Implementation of server-details command."""
  1326→    manager = cli_context.get_manager()
  1327→    
  1328→    console.print(f"[blue]🔍 Getting details for server: {server_name}[/blue]")
  1329→    console.print()
  1330→    
  1331→    # Get detailed server information
  1332→    details = await manager.get_server_details(server_name)
  1333→    
  1334→    if not details:
  1335→        console.print(f"[red]❌ Server '{server_name}' not found[/red]")
  1336→        console.print()
  1337→        
  1338→        # Show available servers
  1339→        servers = await manager.list_servers()
  1340→        if servers:
  1341→            console.print("[yellow]💡 Available servers:[/yellow]")
  1342→            for server in servers:
  1343→                console.print(f"  • {server.name} ({server.server_type.value})")
  1344→        else:
  1345→            console.print("[yellow]💡 No servers configured[/yellow]")
  1346→        return
  1347→    
  1348→    # Display server details
  1349→    from rich.table import Table
  1350→    from rich.panel import Panel
  1351→    from rich import box
  1352→    
  1353→    # Server header
  1354→    status_color = "green" if details['status'] == "enabled" else "red"
  1355→    console.print(Panel(
  1356→        f"[bold cyan]{details['name']}[/bold cyan] - [{status_color}]{details['status'].upper()}[/{status_color}]",
  1357→        title="📦 MCP Server Details",
  1358→        style="blue",
  1359→        box=box.ROUNDED
  1360→    ))
  1361→    console.print()
  1362→    
  1363→    # Basic information table
  1364→    info_table = Table(
  1365→        title="Server Information",
  1366→        box=box.ROUNDED,
  1367→        show_header=True,
  1368→        header_style="bold white on blue"
  1369→    )
  1370→    info_table.add_column("Property", style="cyan", width=15)
  1371→    info_table.add_column("Value", style="white")
  1372→    
  1373→    info_table.add_row("Name", details['name'])
  1374→    info_table.add_row("Type", details['type'])
  1375→    info_table.add_row("Scope", details.get('scope', 'unknown'))
  1376→    info_table.add_row("Status", f"[{status_color}]{details['status']}[/{status_color}]")
  1377→    info_table.add_row("Command", details.get('command', 'N/A'))
  1378→    
  1379→    if details.get('args'):
  1380→        args_str = ' '.join(details['args']) if isinstance(details['args'], list) else str(details['args'])
  1381→        info_table.add_row("Arguments", args_str)
  1382→    
  1383→    if details.get('env'):
  1384→        env_count = len(details['env']) if isinstance(details['env'], dict) else 0
  1385→        info_table.add_row("Environment", f"{env_count} variables")
  1386→    
  1387→    console.print(info_table)
  1388→    console.print()
  1389→    
  1390→    # Tools information
  1391→    tool_count = details.get('tool_count', 'Unknown')
  1392→    tools = details.get('tools', [])
  1393→    source = details.get('source', 'unknown')
  1394→    
  1395→    if tool_count != 'Unknown' and isinstance(tool_count, int) and tool_count > 0:
  1396→        console.print(f"[bold green]🔧 {tool_count} Tools Available[/bold green] [dim]({source})[/dim]")
  1397→        console.print()
  1398→        
  1399→        if tools:
  1400→            tools_table = Table(
  1401→                title="Available Tools",
  1402→                box=box.ROUNDED,
  1403→                show_header=True,
  1404→                header_style="bold white on green"
  1405→            )
  1406→            tools_table.add_column("#", style="dim", width=4, justify="center")
  1407→            tools_table.add_column("Tool Name", style="cyan", width=25)
  1408→            tools_table.add_column("Description", style="white")
  1409→            
  1410→            for i, tool in enumerate(tools, 1):
  1411→                tool_name = tool.get('name', f'Tool {i}')
  1412→                tool_desc = tool.get('description', 'No description available')
  1413→                tools_table.add_row(str(i), tool_name, tool_desc)
  1414→            
  1415→            console.print(tools_table)
  1416→        else:
  1417→            console.print("[dim]Individual tool names not available - tools accessible via MCP protocol[/dim]")
  1418→        
  1419→        console.print()
  1420→        
  1421→        # Usage examples
  1422→        console.print("[bold]💡 Usage in Claude Code:[/bold]")
  1423→        
  1424→        if details['type'] == 'docker-desktop':
  1425→            console.print("[dim]These tools are available via Docker Desktop MCP integration:[/dim]")
  1426→            console.print(f"  [yellow]@{details['name']} <tool-command>[/yellow]")
  1427→            console.print()
  1428→            
  1429→            console.print("[cyan]General usage:[/cyan]")
  1430→            console.print(f"  [yellow]@{details['name']} <command> [arguments][/yellow]")
  1431→            console.print(f"  [yellow]@{details['name']} help[/yellow] - Show available commands")
  1432→        else:
  1433→            console.print(f"[dim]General MCP server usage:[/dim]")
  1434→            console.print(f"  [yellow]@{details['name']} <command>[/yellow]")
  1435→            
  1436→    elif tool_count == 'Unknown':
  1437→        console.print(f"[yellow]🔧 Tool Information Not Available[/yellow] [dim]({source})[/dim]")
  1438→        console.print()
  1439→        
  1440→        # Enhanced display for Docker containers
  1441→        if source == "docker_container_introspection_failed":
  1442→            fallback_info = details.get('fallback_info', {})
  1443→            docker_image = details.get('docker_image')
  1444→            
  1445→            console.print("[dim]Docker container tool discovery failed.[/dim]")
  1446→            
  1447→            if docker_image:
  1448→                console.print(f"[dim]Docker Image: {docker_image}[/dim]")
  1449→            
  1450→            # Show likely tools if available
  1451→            likely_tools = fallback_info.get('likely_tools', [])
  1452→            if likely_tools:
  1453→                console.print()
  1454→                console.print("[bold cyan]🔍 Likely Available Tools:[/bold cyan]")
  1455→                
  1456→                tools_table = Table(
  1457→                    box=box.SIMPLE,
  1458→                    show_header=True,
  1459→                    header_style="bold cyan"
  1460→                )
  1461→                tools_table.add_column("Tool", style="green", width=20)
  1462→                tools_table.add_column("Description", style="white")
  1463→                
  1464→                for tool in likely_tools:
  1465→                    tools_table.add_row(tool['name'], tool['description'])
  1466→                
  1467→                console.print(tools_table)
  1468→            
  1469→            # Show troubleshooting suggestions
  1470→            suggestions = fallback_info.get('suggestions', [])
  1471→            if suggestions:
  1472→                console.print()
  1473→                console.print("[bold cyan]💡 Troubleshooting:[/bold cyan]")
  1474→                for suggestion in suggestions:
  1475→                    console.print(f"  [dim]• {suggestion}[/dim]")
  1476→        else:
  1477→            console.print("[dim]This server type does not provide detailed tool information.[/dim]")
  1478→            console.print(f"[dim]Try using:[/dim] [yellow]@{details['name']} help[/yellow]")
  1479→        
  1480→    else:
  1481→        console.print(f"[red]⚠️ No Tools Detected[/red] [dim]({source})[/dim]")
  1482→        console.print()
  1483→        console.print("[dim]This may indicate a server configuration issue.[/dim]")
  1484→        console.print("Consider checking the server configuration or status.")
  1485→
  1486→
  1487→@cli.command()
  1488→@click.argument("name")
  1489→@click.option(
  1490→    "--interactive", "-i",
  1491→    is_flag=True,
  1492→    help="Interactive configuration mode with prompts"
  1493→)
  1494→@click.option(
  1495→    "--show", "-s",
  1496→    is_flag=True,
  1497→    help="Show current configuration without modifying"
  1498→)
  1499→@handle_errors
  1500→def configure(name: str, interactive: bool, show: bool):
  1501→    """Configure or reconfigure an MCP server that requires additional settings.
  1502→    
  1503→    This command allows you to:
  1504→    - View current configuration for servers like filesystem, SQLite, PostgreSQL
  1505→    - Modify configuration interactively 
  1506→    - Update Docker Desktop MCP server settings
  1507→    
  1508→    Examples:
  1509→      mcp-manager configure filesystem --interactive
  1510→      mcp-manager configure SQLite --show
  1511→      mcp-manager configure postgresql --interactive
  1512→    """
  1513→    asyncio.run(_configure_impl(name, interactive, show))
  1514→
  1515→
  1516→async def _configure_impl(name: str, interactive: bool, show: bool):
  1517→    """Implementation of configure command."""
  1518→    import os
  1519→    import yaml
  1520→    from pathlib import Path
  1521→    from rich.prompt import Prompt, Confirm
  1522→    
  1523→    manager = cli_context.get_manager()
  1524→    
  1525→    console.print(f"[bold blue]🔧 Configuring MCP Server: {name}[/bold blue]")
  1526→    
  1527→    # Get current server configuration
  1528→    servers = await manager.list_servers()
  1529→    target_server = next((s for s in servers if s.name == name), None)
  1530→    
  1531→    if not target_server:
  1532→        console.print(f"[red]✗[/red] Server '{name}' not found")
  1533→        console.print("[yellow]💡[/yellow] Available servers:")
  1534→        for server in servers:
  1535→            console.print(f"  • {server.name} ({server.server_type.value})")
  1536→        return
  1537→    
  1538→    console.print(f"[cyan]Server Type:[/cyan] {target_server.server_type.value}")
  1539→    console.print(f"[cyan]Current Command:[/cyan] {target_server.command}")
  1540→    
  1541→    # Check if this is a configurable server
  1542→    configurable_servers = {
  1543→        'filesystem': {
  1544→            'description': 'Filesystem access requires specifying allowed directories',
  1545→            'config_type': 'docker_mcp' if 'docker' in target_server.command else 'args',
  1546→            'settings': ['directory_paths']
  1547→        },
  1548→        'sqlite': {
  1549→            'description': 'SQLite server requires a database file path',
  1550→            'config_type': 'docker_mcp' if 'docker' in target_server.command else 'args',
  1551→            'settings': ['db_path']
  1552→        },
  1553→        'postgresql': {
  1554→            'description': 'PostgreSQL server requires database connection details',
  1555→            'config_type': 'args',
  1556→            'settings': ['connection_string']
  1557→        }
  1558→    }
  1559→    
  1560→    # Find matching configurable server
  1561→    config_info = None
  1562→    for key, info in configurable_servers.items():
  1563→        if key in name.lower():
  1564→            config_info = info
  1565→            break
  1566→    
  1567→    if not config_info:
  1568→        console.print(f"[yellow]⚠[/yellow] Server '{name}' does not require additional configuration")
  1569→        console.print(f"[dim]Current configuration is sufficient for this server type[/dim]")
  1570→        return
  1571→    
  1572→    console.print(f"[blue]ℹ[/blue] {config_info['description']}")
  1573→    
  1574→    # Show current configuration
  1575→    if config_info['config_type'] == 'docker_mcp':
  1576→        # Docker Desktop MCP server - check config.yaml
  1577→        docker_config_file = Path.home() / ".docker" / "mcp" / "config.yaml"
  1578→        current_config = {}
  1579→        
  1580→        if docker_config_file.exists():
  1581→            try:
  1582→                with open(docker_config_file, 'r') as f:
  1583→                    docker_config = yaml.safe_load(f) or {}
  1584→                    current_config = docker_config.get(name, {})
  1585→            except Exception as e:
  1586→                console.print(f"[yellow]⚠[/yellow] Could not read Docker MCP config: {e}")
  1587→        
  1588→        console.print(f"\n[bold]Current Docker MCP Configuration:[/bold]")
  1589→        if current_config:
  1590→            console.print(yaml.dump({name: current_config}, default_flow_style=False))
  1591→        else:
  1592→            console.print(f"[dim]No configuration found for {name}[/dim]")
  1593→        
  1594→        if show:
  1595→            return
  1596→            
  1597→        if not interactive:
  1598→            console.print(f"[yellow]💡[/yellow] Use --interactive to modify configuration")
  1599→            console.print(f"[yellow]💡[/yellow] Or edit directly: {docker_config_file}")
  1600→            return
  1601→        
  1602→        # Interactive configuration for Docker MCP servers
  1603→        if 'filesystem' in name.lower():
  1604→            console.print(f"\n[bold]Configure Filesystem Paths:[/bold]")
  1605→            console.print(f"[dim]Current paths: {current_config.get('paths', ['None configured'])}[/dim]")
  1606→            
  1607→            if Confirm.ask("Modify filesystem paths?"):
  1608→                new_paths = []
  1609→                console.print(f"[blue]Enter directory paths (press Enter with empty path to finish):[/blue]")
  1610→                
  1611→                # Add current paths as defaults
  1612→                existing_paths = current_config.get('paths', [])
  1613→                for i, path in enumerate(existing_paths):
  1614→                    console.print(f"[dim]Current path {i+1}: {path}[/dim]")
  1615→                    new_path = Prompt.ask(f"Path {i+1}", default=path)
  1616→                    if new_path.strip():
  1617→                        new_paths.append(os.path.expanduser(new_path.strip()))
  1618→                
  1619→                # Add new paths
  1620→                path_num = len(existing_paths) + 1
  1621→                while True:
  1622→                    new_path = Prompt.ask(f"Path {path_num} (empty to finish)", default="")
  1623→                    if not new_path.strip():
  1624→                        break
  1625→                    new_paths.append(os.path.expanduser(new_path.strip()))
  1626→                    path_num += 1
  1627→                
  1628→                if new_paths:
  1629→                    # Update Docker MCP config
  1630→                    docker_config_file.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
  1631→                    
  1632→                    full_config = {}
  1633→                    if docker_config_file.exists():
  1634→                        try:
  1635→                            with open(docker_config_file, 'r') as f:
  1636→                                full_config = yaml.safe_load(f) or {}
  1637→                        except:
  1638→                            pass
  1639→                    
  1640→                    full_config[name] = {'paths': new_paths, 'env': {}}
  1641→                    
  1642→                    with open(docker_config_file, 'w') as f:
  1643→                        yaml.dump(full_config, f, default_flow_style=False)
  1644→                    
  1645→                    console.print(f"[green]✓[/green] Updated filesystem paths: {new_paths}")
  1646→                    console.print(f"[green]📁[/green] Configuration saved to: {docker_config_file}")
  1647→                else:
  1648→                    console.print(f"[yellow]No paths specified - configuration unchanged[/yellow]")
  1649→        
  1650→        elif 'sqlite' in name.lower():
  1651→            console.print(f"\n[bold]Configure SQLite Database:[/bold]")
  1652→            current_db = current_config.get('args', [])
  1653→            if current_db and len(current_db) >= 2:
  1654→                current_path = current_db[1]  # --db-path VALUE
  1655→            else:
  1656→                current_path = "/tmp/mcp-database.db"
  1657→            
  1658→            console.print(f"[dim]Current database: {current_path}[/dim]")
  1659→            
  1660→            if Confirm.ask("Modify database path?"):
  1661→                new_db_path = Prompt.ask("Database file path", default=current_path)
  1662→                new_db_path = os.path.expanduser(new_db_path.strip())
  1663→                
  1664→                # Ensure directory exists
  1665→                os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(new_db_path), exist_ok=True)
  1666→                
  1667→                # Create database if it doesn't exist
  1668→                if not os.path.exists(new_db_path):
  1669→                    import sqlite3
  1670→                    with sqlite3.connect(new_db_path):
  1671→                        pass
  1672→                    console.print(f"[green]✓[/green] Created database file: {new_db_path}")
  1673→                
  1674→                # Update Docker MCP config
  1675→                docker_config_file.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
  1676→                
  1677→                full_config = {}
  1678→                if docker_config_file.exists():
  1679→                    try:
  1680→                        with open(docker_config_file, 'r') as f:
  1681→                            full_config = yaml.safe_load(f) or {}
  1682→                    except:
  1683→                        pass
  1684→                
  1685→                full_config[name] = {
  1686→                    'args': ['--db-path', new_db_path],
  1687→                    'env': {}
  1688→                }
  1689→                
  1690→                with open(docker_config_file, 'w') as f:
  1691→                    yaml.dump(full_config, f, default_flow_style=False)
  1692→                
  1693→                console.print(f"[green]✓[/green] Updated database path: {new_db_path}")
  1694→                console.print(f"[green]📁[/green] Configuration saved to: {docker_config_file}")
  1695→        
  1696→    else:
  1697→        # Non-Docker server - show args
  1698→        console.print(f"\n[bold]Current Arguments:[/bold] {target_server.args}")
  1699→        
  1700→        if show:
  1701→            return
  1702→            
  1703→        console.print(f"[yellow]💡[/yellow] This server uses command-line arguments")
  1704→        console.print(f"[yellow]💡[/yellow] Use 'mcp-manager remove {name}' and 'mcp-manager add {name} <new-command>' to reconfigure")
  1705→
  1706→
  1707→@cli.command("sync")
  1708→@click.option(
  1709→    "--dry-run",
  1710→    is_flag=True,
  1711→    help="Show what would be synchronized without making changes"
  1712→)
  1713→@click.option(
  1714→    "--auto-apply",
  1715→    is_flag=True,
  1716→    help="Automatically apply detected changes without prompts"
  1717→)
  1718→@handle_errors
  1719→def sync_external(dry_run: bool, auto_apply: bool):
  1720→    """Synchronize with external MCP configuration changes.
  1721→    
  1722→    Detects changes made by external tools (docker mcp, claude mcp) and
  1723→    synchronizes the local MCP Manager catalog to match.
  1724→    
  1725→    Examples:
  1726→      mcp-manager sync              # Interactive sync with prompts
  1727→      mcp-manager sync --dry-run    # Show changes without applying
  1728→      mcp-manager sync --auto-apply # Apply all changes automatically
  1729→    """
  1730→    asyncio.run(_sync_external_impl(dry_run, auto_apply))
  1731→
  1732→
  1733→async def _sync_external_impl(dry_run: bool, auto_apply: bool):
  1734→    """Implementation of sync command."""
  1735→    from rich.prompt import Confirm
  1736→    from rich.panel import Panel
  1737→    from rich import box
  1738→    
  1739→    manager = cli_context.get_manager()
  1740→    console.print("[bold blue]🔄 External Configuration Sync[/bold blue]")
  1741→    console.print()
  1742→    
  1743→    # Detect changes
  1744→    console.print("[blue]🔍 Detecting external changes...[/blue]")
  1745→    changes = await detect_external_changes(manager)
  1746→    
  1747→    if not changes:
  1748→        console.print("[green]✅ No external changes detected - configurations are in sync[/green]")
  1749→        return
  1750→    
  1751→    console.print(f"[yellow]📋 Detected {len(changes)} configuration changes:[/yellow]")
  1752→    console.print()
  1753→    
  1754→    # Group changes by source
  1755→    changes_by_source = {}
  1756→    for change in changes:
  1757→        source = change.source.value
  1758→        if source not in changes_by_source:
  1759→            changes_by_source[source] = []
  1760→        changes_by_source[source].append(change)
  1761→    
  1762→    # Display changes by source
  1763→    for source, source_changes in changes_by_source.items():
  1764→        source_name = {
  1765→            'docker': 'Docker Desktop MCP',
  1766→            'claude_user': 'Claude User Config',
  1767→            'claude_project': 'Claude Project Config',
  1768→            'claude_internal': 'Claude Internal Config'
  1769→        }.get(source, source)
  1770→        
  1771→        console.print(Panel(
  1772→            f"[bold cyan]{len(source_changes)} changes[/bold cyan]",
  1773→            title=f"📦 {source_name}",
  1774→            style="cyan",
  1775→            box=box.ROUNDED
  1776→        ))
  1777→        
  1778→        # Create changes table
  1779→        changes_table = Table(
  1780→            box=box.SIMPLE,
  1781→            show_header=True,
  1782→            header_style="bold cyan"
  1783→        )
  1784→        changes_table.add_column("Change", style="yellow", width=15)
  1785→        changes_table.add_column("Server", style="green", width=20)
  1786→        changes_table.add_column("Details", style="white")
  1787→        
  1788→        for change in source_changes:
  1789→            change_desc = {
  1790→                'server_added': '➕ Added',
  1791→                'server_removed': '➖ Removed',
  1792→                'server_modified': '🔄 Modified',
  1793→                'server_enabled': '✅ Enabled',
  1794→                'server_disabled': '❌ Disabled'
  1795→            }.get(change.change_type.value, change.change_type.value)
  1796→            
  1797→            # Format details
  1798→            details_parts = []
  1799→            if 'command' in change.details:
  1800→                details_parts.append(f"cmd: {change.details['command']}")
  1801→            if 'reason' in change.details:
  1802→                details_parts.append(f"({change.details['reason']})")
  1803→            
  1804→            details = ', '.join(details_parts) if details_parts else 'No details'
  1805→            
  1806→            changes_table.add_row(change_desc, change.server_name, details)
  1807→        
  1808→        console.print(changes_table)
  1809→        console.print()
  1810→    
  1811→    if dry_run:
  1812→        console.print("[blue]🔍 Dry run mode - no changes applied[/blue]")
  1813→        return
  1814→    
  1815→    # Apply changes
  1816→    if not auto_apply:
  1817→        if not Confirm.ask("Apply these changes to synchronize configurations?"):
  1818→            console.print("[yellow]⏸️ Synchronization cancelled by user[/yellow]")
  1819→            return
  1820→    
  1821→    console.print("[blue]🔄 Applying synchronization changes...[/blue]")
  1822→    
  1823→    success_count = 0
  1824→    error_count = 0
  1825→    
  1826→    for change in changes:
  1827→        try:
  1828→            change_desc = f"{change.change_type.value} {change.server_name}"
  1829→            
  1830→            if change.change_type.value == 'server_added':
  1831→                # Add server to catalog based on external configuration
  1832→                server_info = change.details.get('server_info', {})
  1833→                command = server_info.get('command', '')
  1834→                args = server_info.get('args', [])
  1835→                env = server_info.get('env', {})
  1836→                
  1837→                # Simple server type detection - don't overthink it
  1838→                if command == 'npx':
  1839→                    server_type = ServerType.NPM
  1840→                elif command.endswith('/docker') or command == 'docker':
  1841→                    server_type = ServerType.CUSTOM  # Let Claude handle Docker servers
  1842→                else:
  1843→                    server_type = ServerType.CUSTOM
  1844→                
  1845→                try:
  1846→                    await manager.add_server(
  1847→                        name=change.server_name,
  1848→                        server_type=server_type,
  1849→                        command=command,
  1850→                        args=args,
  1851→                        env=env,
  1852→                        scope=ServerScope.USER
  1853→                    )
  1854→                    console.print(f"  ✅ Added server: {change.server_name}")
  1855→                except Exception as e:
  1856→                    # If server already exists in Claude, just add to catalog
  1857→                    if "already exists" in str(e).lower():
  1858→                        catalog = await manager._get_server_catalog()
  1859→                        servers = catalog.setdefault('servers', {})
  1860→                        servers[change.server_name] = {
  1861→                            'name': change.server_name,
  1862→                            'type': server_type.value,
  1863→                            'command': command,
  1864→                            'args': args,
  1865→                            'env': env,
  1866→                            'enabled': True,
  1867→                            'scope': 'user'
  1868→                        }
  1869→                        await manager._save_server_catalog(catalog)
  1870→                        console.print(f"  ✅ Synced server to catalog: {change.server_name}")
  1871→                    else:
  1872→                        raise
  1873→                
  1874→            elif change.change_type.value == 'server_removed':
  1875→                # For servers that don't exist externally, remove from catalog directly
  1876→                # This handles cases where servers were removed externally and we need to sync our catalog
  1877→                try:
  1878→                    # First try regular removal (works if server exists in Claude)
  1879→                    await manager.remove_server(change.server_name)
  1880→                    console.print(f"  ➖ Removed server: {change.server_name}")
  1881→                except Exception as e:
  1882→                    # If regular removal fails, remove from catalog directly
  1883→                    logger.debug(f"Regular removal failed: {e}, removing from catalog directly")
  1884→                    catalog = await manager._get_server_catalog()
  1885→                    servers = catalog.get('servers', {})
  1886→                    if change.server_name in servers:
  1887→                        del servers[change.server_name]
  1888→                        await manager._save_server_catalog(catalog)
  1889→                        console.print(f"  ➖ Removed server from catalog: {change.server_name}")
  1890→                    else:
  1891→                        raise
  1892→                
  1893→            elif change.change_type.value in ['server_enabled', 'server_disabled']:
  1894→                enabled = change.change_type.value == 'server_enabled'
  1895→                # Update server status in catalog
  1896→                await manager._update_server_status(change.server_name, enabled)
  1897→                status = "enabled" if enabled else "disabled"
  1898→                console.print(f"  🔄 {change.server_name}: {status}")
  1899→                
  1900→            success_count += 1
  1901→            
  1902→        except Exception as e:
  1903→            console.print(f"  ❌ Failed to apply change for {change.server_name}: {e}")
  1904→            error_count += 1
  1905→    
  1906→    # Summary
  1907→    console.print()
  1908→    if success_count > 0:
  1909→        console.print(f"[green]✅ Successfully applied {success_count} changes[/green]")
  1910→    if error_count > 0:
  1911→        console.print(f"[red]❌ Failed to apply {error_count} changes[/red]")
  1912→    
  1913→    console.print("[blue]🎉 Synchronization complete[/blue]")
  1914→
  1915→
  1916→@cli.command("detect-changes")
  1917→@click.option(
  1918→    "--watch",
  1919→    is_flag=True,
  1920→    help="Continuously monitor for changes (press Ctrl+C to stop)"
  1921→)
  1922→@click.option(
  1923→    "--interval",
  1924→    type=int,
  1925→    default=5,
  1926→    help="Watch interval in seconds (default: 5)"
  1927→)
  1928→@handle_errors
  1929→def detect_changes(watch: bool, interval: int):
  1930→    """Detect external MCP configuration changes.
  1931→    
  1932→    Monitor changes made by external tools like 'docker mcp' and 'claude mcp'
  1933→    commands without applying them.
  1934→    
  1935→    Examples:
  1936→      mcp-manager detect-changes           # One-time change detection
  1937→      mcp-manager detect-changes --watch   # Continuous monitoring
  1938→    """
  1939→    asyncio.run(_detect_changes_impl(watch, interval))
  1940→
  1941→
  1942→async def _detect_changes_impl(watch: bool, interval: int):
  1943→    """Implementation of detect-changes command."""
  1944→    import time
  1945→    from rich.live import Live
  1946→    from rich.panel import Panel
  1947→    from rich import box
  1948→    
  1949→    manager = cli_context.get_manager()
  1950→    detector = ChangeDetector(manager)
  1951→    
  1952→    if not watch:
  1953→        # Single detection
  1954→        console.print("[blue]🔍 Detecting external configuration changes...[/blue]")
  1955→        changes = await detector.detect_changes()
  1956→        
  1957→        if not changes:
  1958→            console.print("[green]✅ No external changes detected[/green]")
  1959→            return
  1960→        
  1961→        console.print(f"[yellow]📋 Detected {len(changes)} changes:[/yellow]")
  1962→        for change in changes:
  1963→            console.print(f"  • {change}")
